document_title: The IC² Institute and Dell Med's AI Learning Lab splits 80 clinicians between Claude and UpToDate with its AI switched off
_note: Caption carried verbatim from caption_winner.txt. Slide strings polished from storyboard.md, each held to its claim quotes in claims.json. Every numeral is in claims.json or figures.json. No slide implies a result or a better group. The AMA figures sit only on S8, attributed to the release (c15).
caption:
Forty clinicians will get Claude. Forty will get UpToDate with its AI switched off.

The split belongs to the AI Learning Lab, announced October 20th by the IC² Institute and Dell Medical School. Its 80 clinicians are faculty, residents and students. Each will meet a paid actor playing a patient.

Researcher Sookja Kang asks how fast clinicians click on their AI tool, whether they accept its output or interrogate it, and how much reasoning gets handed off. The release reports no findings.

What the release does cite is a 2026 American Medical Association survey, with 81% of doctors using AI against 38% in 2023. Vice Dean of Education James Korndorffer says AI is going to be used and should be.

Which of Kang's questions should a Texas medical school see answered before AI enters its curriculum?

#DellMed #ClinicalReasoning #MedicalEducation

S1.headline: Half of them will get Claude
S1.body: 80 Dell Med clinicians will meet paid actors presenting a medical issue. Half will have Claude to help diagnose. The other half will rely on UpToDate with its AI capability disabled. Rooms drawn to illustrate.

S7.headline: How much reasoning gets handed off?

S9.headline: Results could shape the curriculum
S9.body: Researchers will compare both groups with rubrics, observation and post encounter interviews. Watch for the results. The release says they could help schools decide how and when AI enters the curriculum. Drawn to illustrate.
